findings.title: HTTP probe timeout does not bound total request time, so /healthz can block indefinitely on slow responses
findings.evidence: The probe passes a single timeout value to requests.get, which in requests only applies to connect/read socket operations rather than enforcing an overall deadline for the whole probe. A dependency that slowly streams bytes or repeatedly stalls can keep the health endpoint blocked well past timeout_seconds, defeating the intended self-check timeout behavior.
findings.recommendation: Enforce a real overall deadline for HTTP probes, for example by measuring elapsed monotonic time around the request and aborting when it exceeds timeout_seconds, or by using a client/mechanism that supports total request deadlines rather than only per-socket timeouts.

findings.title: HTTP probe treats normal 3xx redirects as failures, which can incorrectly mark healthy dependencies down
findings.evidence: The probe claims to succeed on any 2xx response, but it unconditionally calls raise_for_status after the GET. In requests, redirects can be disabled by a supplied http_get implementation or can terminate in a non-2xx 3xx response, causing the health check to report down even though the service is reachable and responding normally.
findings.recommendation: Define and implement the intended contract explicitly: either accept 3xx as healthy for reachability checks, or force redirect following and validate the final response code. Add tests covering redirect responses so the endpoint behavior is stable.
